opening.headline: How long does the prompt and response sent via the LLM API remain stored on the provider's side? Can you put that simply?
body: Let's assume we operate a service that sends customer inquiries to an LLM API for summarization. Often, after a call ends, team members do not know exactly where the prompt and response are stored or how long they are retained. Retention periods vary by provider, feature, and contract type.

This course compares the basic retention approach with the no-retention (ZDR) option, based on documentation from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, and distinguishes the types of data that are stored. It also verifies exceptions where enabling no-retention does not apply, and explains cases where retention requirements are mapped to corresponding options.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the API retention period and the no-retention option
Can respond to preservation requirements and provider options

screens.title: I don't know how much input data will remain.
screens.lead: As an example, let's examine where one API call's data might be stored in a customer inquiry summary service.

visual.alt: Diagram showing one data path and three potential data retention points marked with question marks for an API call.

paragraphs: There is a service that sends customer inquiry content to an LLM API for summarization. The call completes in just a few seconds, but no one on the team knows exactly where and how much the prompt and response are stored after the call ends, because no one has reviewed the contract or documentation.

In practice, retention periods vary by company, by function within the same company, and by contract type. Therefore, the case where retention is simply summarized as "no retention" is rare. There are logs that record requests and responses, some functions store separate state information to perform operations, and there is also a layer that records account activities.
The questions this class raises are two: What preservation options meet our requirements, and are there any exceptions to those options?

callout.label: Note
callout.text: The values and conditions for this course are based on the content stated in each provider's public documentation. Contract and approval conditions are aspects that must be directly verified with the provider.

screens.outro: Let us begin by recalling our side's logs.

screens.title: Recall where and for how long our API call logs are retained.
screens.lead: When you select a question, the instructor's thought process is displayed. Please try answering it yourself before clicking.

items.prompt: Is the original prompt being logged in our application logs?
items.answer: Regardless of the provider's retention policy, our service logs also store data. It is common practice to record request bodies exactly as they are for debugging purposes. If you only review the provider's side and feel satisfied, the original request may remain stored on our side for a long time.

items.prompt: Has anyone ever checked the contract or documentation to see what remains for the API provider?
items.answer: The document lists basic retention policies, no-retention options, and exceptions, categorized by function. If you have not verified this before, starting with understanding what the default values are is the first step. The following screen compares the three providers in a table format.

items.prompt: Does signing a non-preserved agreement mean all features become non-preserved?
items.answer: Many people believe this, but zero-copy applies only to eligible functions. Functions that require state preservation often fail when the target is removed. This misconception is the central topic of this class.

screens.outro: I will compare the basic retention methods of the three providers in a table.

screens.title: Three providers' basic preserved and non-preserved options
screens.lead: The following table compares the default retention and no-retention options specified in Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google's documentation. Please note that each column has different criteria and read carefully.

data.caption: Provider-specific API default retention policy and no-retention option
rows: Dialogue content including prompts and outputs is not retained by default. However, certain models designated as Covered Models require retention for 30 days.

ZDR is enabled at the organizational level, and each new organization requires the account team to separately enable it. Once enabled, responses are returned, and neither prompts nor responses are stored.
Abuse monitoring logs are generated by default for all API features and are retained for up to 30 days.
Either Modified Abuse Monitoring or ZDR can be selected, and both require prior approval. In ZDR, regardless of the request value `store` being set to `true`, it is always processed as `false`.
The developer-owned logs of the Gemini API are retained by default for a maximum of 55 days, and in AI Studio, they can be adjusted to 7 days, 14 days, 28 days, or 55 days.
The Agent Platform must take actions such as prompt logging, search grounding logs, and so on, per domain, to achieve non-preservation.
data.notes: All three providers state that they do not use the data as a basis for model training. Therefore, the central issue of this course is not training, but rather data retention and retention duration. Even when the period is the same at 30 days, the meaning differs. Anthropic's 30-day period is a mandatory requirement for a specific model, while OpenAI's 30-day period serves as the baseline duration for abuse monitoring logs. Gemini API logs are an optional feature that project owners can enable, and are separately explained from retention for abuse monitoring purposes.

screens.outro: Having verified the basic retention and options, let's now distinguish what type of data is being stored.

screens.title: Types of data being stored
screens.lead: Hover over or select an underlined term in the description below to see a short description. Check the terms one by one.

data.text: The data remaining in the API can be broadly categorized into two types. The first is Misuse Monitoring Logs. This log may include customer content such as prompts and responses, as well as metadata derived from that content, such as classification results. The second is Application State. This refers to data that some API features store while performing their operations, and may remain until explicitly deleted. Anthropic states that it retains only the data necessary for each feature's functionality and explicitly specifies TTL in each feature's documentation. Features that store state are often not subject to deletion policies. Additionally, when using a Claude Code API key, data retention does not apply; however, if Indicator logging is enabled, usage statistics and similar data may be retained.

terms.tip: Logs generated to detect policy violations. The OpenAI documentation states that these logs can contain derived metadata such as prompts, responses, and classifier results.
Some API features store data to process requests. There are also items that remain until deleted, such as conversations or threads.
This is the time limit for data retention. Anthropic specifies this value in each feature's documentation for features that require data preservation.
This is a setting to record Claude Code usage statistics. When enabled, productivity data will be excluded from retention and may be preserved.

screens.outro: Since we have distinguished the storage types, let us now specifically examine the exceptions where no retention applies.

screens.title: Exceptions where no preservation is applied
screens.lead: The next card describes five exceptions where data persists even when non-preservation is enabled. Select a card to flip it. Use the right arrow to proceed to the next card.

cards.back: In Anthropic's functionality eligibility matrix, features marked as "No" are not subject to sandboxing as in code execution. While such features can be used, at the moment of use, the data follows the retention policy of the feature itself. OpenAI also states that even with ZDR enabled, applications cannot save application state for ineligible endpoints.

Using search grounding stores query logs for up to 3 days, and this storage cannot be deleted. With map grounding, prompts and generated outputs are stored for 30 days. The Interactions API defaults to `true` for all models if `store` is not specified; to enable no retention, `store = false` must be explicitly specified.

cards.front: A model where preservation is essential
cards.back: Anthropic's Covered Models require a 30-day retention period and cannot be used without retention approval. If an organization has incorrect retention settings attempts to access this model, `400 invalid_request_error` will be returned. ZDR organizations can use this model by enabling a 30-day retention period only for specific workspaces.

There is no retention policy other than no retention. For example, Anthropic's activity feed is retained for six years, and local session logs are also stored by default for six years. Resources such as state storage for Claude Console usage and Claude Managed Agents are not subject to retention.

Even with no retention or HIPAA settings, content that is legally required to be retained or flagged by automated safety systems may be preserved. Anthropic advises that flagged conversations or sessions may be retained for up to two years. If handling medical information, it is advised to use HIPAA readiness rather than no retention.

screens.outro: Having verified all exceptions, we will now proceed with an example demonstrating how requirements and options are matched.

screens.title: Case Explanation: Matching Preservation Requirements with Options
screens.lead: The instructor demonstrates how preservation requirements are mapped to options. Select an arrow to proceed step by step.

steps.title: Request is stated in sentences.
steps.body: The requirement is "the original customer inquiry is not stored on the provider's server, only indicators for fault analysis are retained on our side." Specifying what is not stored and where it is not stored provides a clear basis for selecting options.

steps.title: List the required features
steps.body: The functionality used by the service involves a single message API call. It does not support file attachments or code execution. Once the exact set of functionalities is known, the scope of potential vulnerabilities to be evaluated is significantly reduced.

steps.title: Compared by provider eligibility
steps.body: If Anthropic, verify whether the message API is within the ZDR scope in the eligibility matrix, and if so, request ZDR at the organizational level. Also include in the schedule that the account team must separately enable ZDR for each new organization. If OpenAI, prior approval is required.

steps.title: Check for exceptions
steps.body: Check whether the system supports file or state persistence. Also verify that the model is not explicitly designated as requiring preservation. If either condition is met, that component will not be preserved but instead will follow the preservation policy of the respective functionality.

steps.title: Draw a conclusion
steps.body: The option that satisfies this requirement is ZDR; adding file attachments to the service violates the requirement. Therefore, this table must be updated each time a new feature is added. Additionally, it is necessary to verify separately whether the original text remains in our application logs.

screens.outro: Having verified the normal path, I will now explain the case where an exception occurs.

screens.title: Case Explanation: Cases Where No-Conservation Is Not Applied
screens.lead: Check the responses for three scenarios where data persists even with non-persistent contracts, depending on the selected tab.

tabs.label: Scenario A
tabs.body: The organization that has entered a ZDR agreement began document processing by enabling the functionality to store state. At that moment, the data follows the retention policy of the functionality itself, not ZDR. Even if the contract states "no retention," data will persist because it is governed by the retention policy of the feature. The appropriate action is to verify, prior to enabling the feature, that the feature is marked as "Yes" in the eligibility matrix.

tabs.label: Scenario B
tabs.body: A specific model is designated as essential for retention and cannot be used within ZDR organizations. Access to an organization's retention settings when they are incorrectly configured returns a 400 error. If this model must be used, the only option is to enable 30-day retention specifically within that workspace, while all other workspaces maintain no retention. The workspace in which the model is used determines the retention scope.

tabs.label: Scenario C
tabs.body: Enabled search grounding in the Google environment to strengthen the basis of the response. This feature stores query logs for up to three days and cannot be disabled. If data retention is required, either disable this feature or review alternative solutions recommended by the documentation. Disabling a feature that cannot be turned off is the only workaround.

screens.outro: The common point among the three scenarios is that the functionality was not verified before being enabled. Now, let's summarize.

screens.title: Integration summary: Options must be verified including functionality to be considered complete.
screens.lead: Let's go back to the first question and clarify: why can't we simply state in one sentence how much data remains?

paragraphs: The retention period for data remaining in APIs varies depending on the provider, feature, and contract type, and therefore cannot be summarized in one sentence. Anthropic turns off data retention at the organizational level by default, without preserving conversation content; OpenAI retains abuse monitoring logs for a maximum of 30 days by default, requiring prior approval for data retention; Google requires specific actions to be taken per domain before data retention can be disabled.

Choosing an option does not end there. There are exceptions for non-retention. Inappropriate functions follow their own retention policies, some logs cannot be exported, and legal obligations or flagged content may be retained separately.

Therefore, it is necessary to develop the habit of documenting requirements in sentences, listing the functions associated with them, and comparing each function against preservation eligibility. This review must be repeated every time a new function is introduced to ensure preservation requirements are met.

checks.intro: Recall the type of stored data you verified a moment ago and respond. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: An organization that has entered a non-preservation (ZDR) agreement enabled the functionality to store status when processing documents. What happens to that data?
options: ZDR is applied and then deleted immediately after response.
Follows the retention policy of the feature itself
It is only recorded in our side logs, not in the provider's logs.
checks.explain: ZDR incompatibility features can be used, but at that moment the data's retention policy is applied to the feature. Therefore, compatibility must be verified before enabling the feature.

wrong.0: The state storage feature is often not applicable to ZDR targets.
wrong.2: The retention period varies by function and is not a uniform 30 days.
wrong.3: The core issue is what remains with the provider.

checks.correctFeedback: Yes. Even if a non-preservation agreement exists, data pertaining to non-compliant functions follows the preservation policy of that function.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Persistence is not automatically applied to all features. Reconsider which features involve state preservation.

checks.intro: Pair up the preservation features of the three providers. Scores are not saved, so feel free to try.
checks.q: Pair the provider with the preservation-related explanation.
right: Actions must be taken on a per-domain basis to address ZDR, and Gemini logs retain a default maximum of 55 days.
Conversation content is not preserved by default, and ZDR is organized on an organizational basis.
Misuse monitoring logs have a default maximum of 30 days, and ZDR requires prior approval.
checks.explain: Each provider has different conditions for basic retention and no-retention options, so they cannot be summarized in one sentence.
checks.correctFeedback: We accurately distinguished the three providers. We properly identified that the default values and approval conditions differ.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Some pairs do not match. Please reconnect them based on the default retention period, the unit that enables no retention, and whether approval is required.

glossary.def: This is the period during which the provider retains request and response data.
An agreement or setting that prevents storing the prompt and response after a response is returned.
This refers to features or data existing outside of non-preserved data, such as separate logs, rather than preserved data.
Some API features store data intended to perform the operation.
Logs generated and retained for detecting policy violations.

misconceptions.myth: Once ZDR is enabled, no functionality remains regardless of what is used.
misconceptions.fact: Functions marked "No" in the eligibility table follow their own retention policy. Eligibility must be verified before enabling a function.

misconceptions.myth: By default, the data is used for model training.
misconceptions.fact: The documents from the three providers state that they are not intended for use in learning. Therefore, the issue is not whether learning occurs, but rather how long the data is retained.

misconceptions.myth: ZDR applies to the entire account once it is enabled.
misconceptions.fact: Anthropic instructs that each organization must be enabled at the organizational level, and a separate account team must enable each new organization. Organizations under the same account do not automatically scale.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: There are exceptions even in non-preservation cases.
The retention period and options vary depending on the provider, feature, and contract type.
Checks eligibility for non-preserving before enabling the function.
Maps requirements to options to identify gaps.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are intended for you to think about on your own and are not submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: What preservation requirements must our service uphold, and among the current features, which ones could potentially violate those requirements?
